h1: Selling imported sodium humate as your humic biostimulant? Your licence may be at risk
title: Sodium humate under FCO: the risk for brands | GBO
desc: FCO humic acid specs name potassium humate. If your humic is sodium humate, your brand may face stop-sale and penal action. How to check and switch.
answer: If the humic acid in your brand is imported sodium humate, it may not match the FCO Schedule VI humic specifications, which describe the ingredient as potassium humate from leonardite. A non-standard product can draw a stop-sale notice, licence action and penal action under the Essential Commodities Act. Check your supplier's certificate now and switch if needed.
sections: What the FCO humic specification actually names

Humic and fulvic acids are regulated as biostimulants under Schedule VI of the Fertiliser Control Order (FCO), 1985. A humic product can be sold only if it meets a notified specification.

The humic acid specifications notified in S.O. 2346(E) of 26 May 2025 describe the active ingredient in these words: "Humic acid (as Potassium humate obtained from Leonardite mineral source) per cent. by weight, minimum". Another grade in the same notification reads "Humic acid powder as potassium humate (Source: Leonardite)". You can see this wording reproduced on a listed manufacturer's product page.

Sodium humate is not a listed form in the humic specifications we reviewed. The humic specifications were revised again by S.O. 876(E) of 16 February 2026, so read the latest gazette for the exact text of your grade. Our explainer on FCO Schedule VI covers the wider rules.
Why so much of the market is sodium humate

Raw humic material does not dissolve in water. It is made soluble with a strong alkali, and that alkali stays in the product.

PointPotassium humateSodium humate
Made withPotassium hydroxide (KOH)Sodium hydroxide (NaOH, caustic soda)
Adds to the cropPotassium, a plant nutrientSodium, which crops do not need
Cost to makeHigherLower
Looks likeBlack powder or shiny flakesBlack powder or shiny flakes
Named in the FCO humic specs we reviewedYesNo

Caustic soda is cheaper than potash. That is why low-priced imported "humic 98%" flakes are often sodium humate. The two look the same in the bag, so a marketer can buy one believing it is the other. A big percentage on the label does not settle it. Our guide on what a 98% humic claim can mean explains why.
What is at stake for the brand owner

The FCO is issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, and Clause 19 bars the manufacture and sale of fertilisers that are not of the prescribed standard. State agriculture departments enforce it through inspectors, samples and lab tests.

In a Lok Sabha answer of 16 December 2025, the Ministry of Agriculture said a violation of the FCO attracts cancellation and suspension of the authorisation letter, and penal action under the Essential Commodities Act with imprisonment of three months to seven years.

For a marketer, the practical risks are:

  • A stop-sale notice on a batch picked up by an inspector.
  • Suspension or cancellation of your authorisation or NOC.
  • Prosecution if the sample is declared non-standard.
  • Dealer and farmer trust, which takes years to rebuild after one failed sample.

Whether action follows in a given case depends on the sample, the lab report and the state. Check with your state agriculture department.
The field side: why repeated sprays matter

Humic is now sprayed every 12 to 15 days on many farms, and every 5 to 7 days on vegetables. One spray of sodium humate at a normal dose carries little sodium. The concern is the build-up over 10 to 20 applications a season, year after year.

Soil scientists have long shown what excess sodium does. An ICAR Indian Farming article from the Central Arid Zone Research Institute explains that high sodium reduces the availability of calcium, magnesium and micronutrients, and leads to soil dispersion, crusting and poor water infiltration. Many farms already irrigate with salty borewell water, which adds to the load.

When a farmer's soil turns hard after seasons of cheap humic, the brand on the bag takes the blame.
Five checks to run on your humic supplier this week

1. Ask in writing: potassium humate or sodium humate? "Humic acid 98%" or just "humate" is not an answer.
  2. Ask for the K2O content. Genuine potassium humate carries measurable potassium.
  3. Ask for the sodium (Na) content on a batch certificate of analysis, from an NABL-accredited lab where possible.
  4. Ask which Schedule VI specification and gazette number the material meets, and the raw material source.
  5. Run a quick flame test in your office. A strong yellow-orange flame points to sodium, a pale lilac flame to potassium. It is a screening check, not a lab result, so confirm with a lab.

If the answers are unclear, send a sample to a lab before your next order, not after an inspector's sample.

faq: Is sodium humate allowed as a biostimulant under FCO?

The humic acid specifications we reviewed, including S.O. 2346(E) of May 2025, describe the ingredient as potassium humate from leonardite. Sodium humate is not a listed form in them. The specs were revised in February 2026, so read the latest gazette and check with your state agriculture department.
What is the penalty for selling a non-standard biostimulant?

The Ministry of Agriculture told the Lok Sabha in December 2025 that FCO violations attract cancellation or suspension of the authorisation letter and penal action under the Essential Commodities Act, with imprisonment of three months to seven years. Check with your state agriculture department.
How can I tell if my humic is sodium humate or potassium humate?

Ask the supplier for K2O and sodium figures on a batch certificate of analysis from an accredited lab. A flame test gives a quick hint: strong yellow-orange points to sodium, pale lilac to potassium. Confirm with a lab.
Does one spray of sodium humate damage the crop?
Usually not at a normal dose. The concern is the sodium that builds up over many sprays a season and many seasons, especially where irrigation water is already salty.
Can I switch my brand from sodium humate to potassium humate?
Yes. Source potassium humate that meets a notified Schedule VI humic specification, get the batch certificate of analysis, and check your label and documents against the grade before you sell.
